suggested_visuals.section_heading: The Three Payback Scenarios Explained — and How Likely Each One Really Is
suggested_visuals.purpose: Let the reader see the three payback periods against a single break-even line, making the spread between scenarios immediately legible without re-reading the arithmetic.
suggested_visuals.alt_text_proposal: Line chart of cumulative net profit over 36 months for three arcade machine scenarios, crossing the $4,250 break-even line at 6.5, 14 and 36 months.
suggested_visuals.production_note: Simple three-line chart, no branding. X-axis 0-36 months, Y-axis $0-$8,000, horizontal dashed line at $4,250. Label crossings 6.5 / 14.0 / 35.9 months.

suggested_visuals.section_heading: The Recurring Costs That Quietly Erode Arcade Profit
suggested_visuals.purpose: Show visually how gross coin drop becomes net profit, so the reader stops treating the two as interchangeable.
suggested_visuals.alt_text_proposal: Waterfall diagram reducing $325 monthly gross arcade drop by a $16.25 service reserve and $5 electricity to $303.75 net profit.
suggested_visuals.production_note: Unbranded waterfall chart, four bars. Include an optional greyed-out 50% revenue-share bar to show the operator-placement variant.

suggested_visuals.section_heading: A Real Machine to Anchor the Math: The JVL ECHO HD3 Commercial Edition
suggested_visuals.purpose: Give the price anchor a physical referent and show the bill and coin hardware that makes the venue revenue model possible.
suggested_visuals.alt_text_proposal: JVL ECHO HD3 Commercial Edition bartop arcade machine on a bar counter, with a close-up inset of its bill acceptor and coin slot.
suggested_visuals.production_note: Real product photo in a bar setting, evening lighting. Inset must clearly show the bill acceptor and quarter coin mech. First and only branded image in the article, per the editorial-imagery rule.
